finding: Literature review finds weak evidence for CBT in CFS; questionnaire follow-up (mean 34 months) of a UK multidisciplinary service; abstract truncated.
Subjective sleep: mean PSQI 10.17 and ESS 10.51; no linear ESS-PSQI relation, and a subgroup (n=69) had an insomnia-like phenotype with low ESS and high PSQI.
Statistical-mechanics model of persistent EBV driving chronic immune activation; no patient data.
Nurse-delivered psychological interventions in primary care raised four challenges (novice therapists, engagement, emotions, primary-care complexity).
PSQI fits a three-factor model in CFS (sleep efficiency, perceived quality, daily disturbances); global PSQI alpha only 0.64.
On incremental tilt, n-back performance deteriorated and neuronally activated CBFV fell in young CFS but not controls; critical closing pressure was higher (raised vasomotor tone).
School-based surveillance found CFS/ME in 1.0% of 2855 children (28), with milder fatigue and disability than health-service-referred cases.
Within a Fukuda-defined cohort, those meeting Canadian ME/CFS or Ramsay-type ME criteria had more impairment and more severe physical and cognitive symptoms.
3T voxel-based morphometry in 26 CFS vs 26 matched controls found regional grey and white matter volume changes; the abstract links them to memory, visual processing and motor planning.

population: CFS with and without orthostatic intolerance
finding: Echocardiography showed smaller LV dimensions, stroke volume index, cardiac index and LV mass in CFS with orthostatic intolerance than in CFS without OI and controls.
BDI-II factor analysis in CFS shows two factors; patients endorse somatic items that overlap with CFS symptoms.
No XMRV/MLV nucleic acids, infectious virus or antibodies in Canadian CFS patients or controls.
Median wait to specialist assessment far exceeded NICE timeframes (1/125 severe seen in time); more fatigue predicted shorter wait.
Adults with CFS/ME describe needs for personalised, timely, sustained health and social care, with barriers especially for disadvantaged groups.
94 Australian CFS patients used 474 different medicines; evidence from RCTs for these is very limited.

population: CFS with or without fibromyalgia, women
finding: Sleep-stage transition analysis: REM-to-wake transitions higher in CFS alone, and several transitions increased in CFS+FM versus controls.
Accelerometry for 6 days: CFS patients were less active and more sedentary than sedentary controls; peak activity and peak/average ratio did not differ.
TGF-beta1 mRNA in PBMCs was higher in 63 CFS than in disease controls and healthy controls.
note: Chinese cohort; mRNA not serum; atlas says serum TGF-b artefact

finding: No XMRV/HMRV/MLV group G3 detected by PCR in white cells of 78 ME/CFS patients or in 168 donor sera.
Systematic review of CAM RCTs: limited evidence overall; qigong, massage and tuina positive, most supplements failed except NADH and magnesium.

population: ME/CFS (Fukuda-type, Belgian); also chronic fatigue group
finding: IL-1, TNF-alpha, neopterin, lysozyme and PMN-elastase were higher in ME/CFS than controls and CF; IL-1 and TNF correlated with fatigue and flu-like malaise.
IgA responses to LPS of commensal enterobacteria were associated with higher IL-1, TNF-alpha, neopterin and elastase and with IBS ratings, suggesting bacterial translocation.
note: Maes; no healthy control group in abstract

finding: Supervised SNP selection yielded a polymorphism profile predicting CFS with the highest reported accuracy on this dataset.
note: Reanalysis of old candidate-SNP dataset; no replication

finding: CFS patients showed more somatic complaints and alexithymic difficulty identifying feelings; depression and obsessive symptoms only in the depressed subgroup.
Tuina over 20 days reduced FACIT fatigue scores; EMG median frequency unchanged by treatment and different only in back muscles versus controls.
note: Uncontrolled for treatment; traditional Chinese medicine

finding: Uncontrolled inpatient CBT plus GET: large effect sizes on fatigue (1.2) and impairment (-0.9); 30-34% clinically improved.

n: CFS vs chronic inflammatory vs healthy
finding: Low-level XMRV PCR signals in 15% of CFS patients were no different from controls and could not be confirmed; no specific antibody.
Lack of acceptance was associated with impaired functioning and fatigue; acceptance increased after CBT.
No XMRV DNA, antibody, antigen or infectious virus found in Quebec CFS patients.
Half (50.1%) of 2170 patients had stopped work due to fatigue symptoms; productivity cost estimated at about 102 million pounds per year.
Patients on long-term sickness absence had more physical fatigue, worse sleep and more embarrassment-avoidance cognitions.
72% of 40 mothers were above GHQ-12 cut-off; families had income loss and added expense.
Kai Xin San herbal formula reduced exhaustion markers in a forced-wheel-running mouse model.
Phylogenetic analysis shows longitudinal MLV sequences from CFS patients are distinct endogenous murine retroviruses, consistent with PCR contamination.
Population-based study: stressors, psychological distress and PTSD were more common in people with CFS than controls.
Latent class analysis found 5 subgroups, all improving with CBT; exploratory regression found one minority class predicting poor outcome.
Data mining: Canadian criteria classified 87% of CFS cases vs 79% for the empiric (Reeves 2005) definition.
In a four-arm non-pharmacological RCT, more homework completion predicted better role, social and mental health function but not fatigue or physical function.
Minimum ME/CFS prevalence 0.2% overall (0.19% CDC-1994, 0.11% Canadian, 0.03% epidemiological); incidence 0.015% per year.
EGCG improved behaviour and oxido-nitrosative markers in a forced-swim rat fatigue model.
Commentary summarising evidence that XMRV was laboratory contamination and absent in the originally positive CFS cohort.
Consecutive series: 91% women, mean age 48; trigger identified in 58%, gradual onset 63%, comorbid anxiety 83%, sicca 82%, fibromyalgia 55%.
No XMRV in PBMCs or plasma of CFS-discordant twins; one plasma positive in an unaffected co-twin not reproduced.
Anxiety and dyadic adjustment correlated with cardioventilatory responses at rest and very low-intensity exercise.
No difference in neuropsychological performance across three illness-duration groups, suggesting non-progressive cognitive impairment.
Childhood maltreatment history did not alter CBT response in CFS but was linked to more limitations and distress.
Radix pseudostellariae polysaccharide lessened poly I:C-induced fatigue and immune changes in mice.
Mitochondrial content was lower in CFS than in controls, but respiratory chain activities corrected for content were not, and CFS had higher ATP production rate than mitochondrial disease.
note: Small; abstract lacks n; likely PBMC/muscle

finding: SF-36 in ME/CFS: physical component 26.8, mental 34.1; carers also impaired.
Seropositivity for Borrelia or EBV in 66%; longer CFS duration associated with higher BMI.
Norwegian newspaper content analysis: statements were mostly positive for Lightning Process and negative for evidence-based treatment.
CFS had poorer emotion recognition than controls but intact emotional theory of mind.
CFS had more PTSD symptoms and trauma exposure than non-fatigued controls, unrelated to fatigue severity.
Systematic review: most PROMs used in CFS/ME have limited validity evidence, other than the SF-36.
Triaxial accelerometry: CFS less active in afternoon/evening, fewer high-intensity and more low-intensity activities, with more within-person variability.
Self-esteem fully mediated the link between maladaptive perfectionism and depression in CFS.
Interviews show specific positive and negative metacognitions about symptom processing in CFS.
SPM voxel-based MRI: midbrain white matter volume fell with fatigue duration, and brainstem volume correlated with pulse pressure, suggesting impaired cerebrovascular autoregulation.
Pilot ME/CFS register: 96.9% of 160 participants met CDC-1994 (Fukuda); Canadian criteria defined a subset.
Newly referred patients hoped for diagnosis, guidance and support, with high uncertainty about the illness.
Modified advanced trail making test discriminated childhood CFS from controls (70.5% accuracy); alternative attention was lower; 6-month CBT plus medication improved status.
No XMRV or MLV sequences, virus or antibodies in 100 CFS patients, 200 controls or original-study samples; mouse DNA in Taq enzymes explained earlier positives.
Premorbid psychopathology at 23 and 33 years raised odds of self-reported CFS/ME (OR 1.85, 2.81); activity extremes were not associated; prevalence 1.0%.
No difference in sleep, activity or diurnal salivary cortisol patterns; low nocturnal heart rate variability correlated with unrefreshing sleep.
Citalopram and imipramine improved behavioural and oxidative markers in a forced swim fatigue model through nitric oxide.
A 10-cytokine/chemokine signature classified XMRV/CFS with 96% sensitivity and 93% specificity.
Pilot study: higher HDAC activity, lower antioxidant power, lower plasma cortisol, higher DHEA and lower glucocorticoid receptor gene expression in elderly CFS.
Network reanalysis of expression, SNP and proteomic data implicated eleven genes, notably WASF3.
Prevalence 111 and incidence 12 per 100,000 adolescents; 91% severely fatigued, 45% missed over half of school.
Danggui Buxue Tang improved endurance and cytokine signalling in a forced-swim rat model.
Editorial: 84% of British neurologists did not view CFS as neurological; discusses classification.
Adolescents show varied, flexible illness beliefs and coping unlike adult findings.
Review hypothesising CFS as chronic brain inflammation and proposing anti-TNF therapy; no new data.
PCR of CSF from 43 CFS patients found no XMRV or other common viruses.
Work and Social Adjustment Scale is reliable and valid for measuring disability in CFS and sensitive to CBT.
Plasma peroxides were higher in ME/CFS than controls; oxLDL antibody showed a trend.
Engagement with pragmatic rehabilitation depended on feeling believed and model concordance.
Commentary on blood donation deferral for people with ME/CFS under XMRV uncertainty.
Review: children with CFS/ME score lower on sustained, switching and divided attention and immediate recall versus norms; coping strategies suggested.
A 44-gene PBMC expression classifier correctly classified only about two-thirds of samples in an independent population, so earlier reporter genes appear study-specific.
CFS prevalence 0.8% in White vs 3.5% in Pakistani group; anxiety, depression, inactivity and social strain were risk factors.
No convincing XMRV antibodies or DNA in CFS patients, donors or prostate cancer patients.
CFS and AN groups had poorer distress tolerance and more self-silencing than controls.
Active energy expenditure (>3 METs) was lower in CFS, with similar sedentary time, and the reduction was partly explained by autonomic dysfunction (HRV) but not fatigue severity.
Migraine in 84% and tension headache in 81% of CFS in cohort 2 versus 5% and 45% of controls; migraine with aura linked to more neuro-symptoms.
Excess of KIR3DS1 and missing KIR2DS5 in CFS, and many KIRs lacking their HLA-Bw4 ligand.
Kindling model of the limbic-hypothalamic-pituitary axis as etiology; no data.
CFS group scored higher on neuroticism and conscientiousness than controls.
Therapist explained 0% of variance in fatigue and under 2% in disability after CBT.
Patent for anti-CD20 antibody use in CFS/ME.
Reduced focusing on fatigue mediated CBT effects on fatigue and impairment; avoidance did not change.
Community CFS prevalence 1.0%; CFS participants slept 5.5 h vs 6.3 h and unrefreshing sleep had sensitivity 92.9% and specificity 87.8%.
Of 32 community CFS cases, 4 died, 16 of 24 re-evaluated still had CFS, 1 remitted; post-exertional malaise best differentiated CFS.
Meta-analysis: exercise therapy appears to reduce fatigue; evidence moderate to low; no adverse effects reported in individualised programmes.
CFS accounted for about 3286 dollars of annual direct medical costs and reduced earnings.
CFS had slower alertness and impaired working, visual and verbal memory versus controls, with less correlation to depression or fatigue than in MDD.
Failure to recover within 1 day after two CPETs 24 h apart had AUC 0.864 (sensitivity 0.80, specificity 0.93) for CFS membership.
Whole blood glutathione peroxidase activity did not differ between ME/CFS and controls, though lower in depression.
Most fatigue scales had sensitivity or specificity problems; the PEM subscale of the ME/CFS Fatigue Types Questionnaire performed best.
CD56 NK cell numbers were lower and IL-6 and IL-2r higher in CFS; BDI and NHP scores higher.
Left third intercostal space tenderness in 81% of 42 ME patients and none of 20 controls.
Thesis on attentional bias to health-threat words and pictures in CFS vs controls; abstract truncated before results.
Self-critical perfectionism related to daily hassles and stress sensitivity, which predicted depression over 14 days (EMA).
PACE mediation analysis using instrumental variables; no abstract in the batch.
Plasma neuropeptide Y was elevated in CFS compared with controls and GWI and correlated with symptom severity.
Systematic review: CFS patients have less daily physical activity and peak isometric strength than sedentary controls, with conflicting but likely reduced exercise capacity.
No difference in BP, HR or skin blood flow responses to mental stress, though baseline HR was higher in CFS.
Attention and executive deficits were present regardless of depression, so cognitive impairment is not secondary to depression.
Lipid peroxidation (MDA) did not differ overall; high-MDA subgroup differed, with lower HDL in CFS.
60% of 260 referrals met Fukuda CFS; others mostly had chronic-disease fatigue or sleep disorders.
Spanish nursing-oriented overview of CFS.
Nursing role in CFS management at a Spanish unit.
Patent for transdermal androgen in fibromyalgia and CFS.
Metacognitions predicted symptom severity better than anxiety or depression.
COMT Rs4680 AA genotype and beta2-adrenergic receptor Rs1042714 genotype frequencies differed from a reference sample in adolescent CFS.
note: Small; reference from NCBI database; p about 0.045

finding: 24-h ambulatory monitoring: night-time HR, mean and diastolic BP higher in adolescent CFS than controls, indicating sympathetic predominance.
Over 4 years fatigue was stable (FIS improved in 39%, worsened ≥10 points in 45%) and independently associated with orthostatic symptoms.
Adolescents with CFS/ME after glandular fever reported lower perceived competency and worse physical functioning and health at 12 and 24 months than recovered peers.
Of 50 interviewed, acupuncture was most often reported as helpful for pain; descriptive only.
Blood nitric oxide was normal and unrelated to activity levels in CFS.
Patients within their energy envelope before treatment improved more in physical function and fatigue after non-drug interventions.
Only maladaptive perfectionism related to fatigue and depression; depression mediated its effect on fatigue.
Pooled daily physical activity in CFS was 68% of controls (14 of 17 studies lower); variability not significantly different.
No XMRV DNA in 32 CFS patients or other groups in Boston.
Qualitative feasibility study concluded a UK ME/CFS post-mortem tissue bank is desirable and acceptable.
Lower HF systolic BP variability and greater shift to sympathetic baroreflex control under -20 mmHg LBNP in adolescent CFS.
Mean time to diagnosis 3.7 years (range 0-34); quality of life fell after onset; patients saw 4.5 services before diagnosis.
No XMRV by multiplex PCR/RT-PCR in 65 Chinese CFS patients or controls.
Clinicians identified psychiatric comorbidity in 44% versus 56% by structured interview; misses outnumbered misdiagnoses.
Children with CFS/ME had higher isoprostanes (252 vs 216 pg/mL) and lower vitamin C, more white cell apoptosis, but normal arterial stiffness.
After 2.2 years, 51.9% had nearly complete symptom improvement and 48.1% did not.
Original WPI group addendum defending XMRV detection (>75% of 101 CFS) and claiming PBMC DNA PCR is least sensitive.
note: Claim later retracted (see atlas); contradicts the refutation

finding: Patent for acylcarnitine diagnosis and supplements for CFS.
Figure-copying tasks show longer reaction and movement time in CFS, with no excess impaired inhibition.
Plasma alpha-MSH was higher in CFS (17.9 vs 14.5 pg/mL, p=0.02) with no correlation to ACTH, cortisol or DHEA-S.
MLV-like gag sequences in 32 of 37 CFS (86.5%) vs 3 of 44 donors; later shown to be contamination.
note: Lo et al. 2010 (PNAS); contradicts refuted-XMRV atlas finding; later retracted

population: Interstitial cystitis with IBS, FM and CFS
finding: Self-reported CFS in 9.5% of interstitial cystitis patients vs 1.7% of controls.
Serum alpha-tocopherol was lower in CFS and rose in remission versus exacerbation, suggesting oxidative stress tracks severity.
29% of CFS had at least one personality disorder vs 7% of well controls (28% in ISF); higher neuroticism.
After glandular fever, 7.8% met CFS criteria at 6 months; anxiety, depression, somatisation, perfectionism and all-or-nothing behaviour predicted onset.
SF-36 Vitality, Role-Physical and Social Functioning best identified substantial functional reduction for CFS case definition.
Review-style article on the WPI XMRV finding; no new data.
Over 2.5 years, comorbid fibromyalgia at baseline raised odds of non-improvement 3.23-fold and somatiser status 3.33-fold.
No XMRV by CDC Western blot, ELISA or PCR in 51 CFS and 56 controls.
Ventricular CSF lactate by 1H MRSI was higher in CFS than healthy volunteers (replicating earlier result) and not different in MDD; correlated with mental fatigue; GABA and Glx unchanged.
Patent for alpha-1-antitrypsin in CFS based on RNase L elastase activity; one patient described.
Focus groups: tailored, self-paced activity felt helpful, whereas non-customised activity caused setbacks.
Self-confrontation method (6 or 12 sessions) improved self-reported fatigue and function, maintained at 10 months.
note: Small; no blinded or passive control

finding: Patent for alpha-1-antitrypsin to treat CFS.
PRIME project built a patient-experience evidence base from 40 interviews.
Orthostatic symptoms (OGS) independently predicted functional impairment in CFS (PROMIS HAQ 36 vs 6 in controls).
Patent for alpha-1-antitrypsin to treat CFS.
Clinical behavioural assessment model for CFS and FM.
Plasma nitrates rose much more with exercise in CFS (up to 295% higher than controls).
Nocturnal HRV was lower in CFS and predicted poor subjective sleep, suggesting sympathetic hypervigilance in sleep.
Olive extract reduced oxidative stress and TNF in an LPS or Brucella fatigue mouse model.
Symptom deterioration occurred in 2-12% on CBT vs 7-17% in controls; no excess harm with CBT.
Cardiac PCr/ATP correlated with muscle bioenergetics, and 4 of 12 CFS had cardiac energy impairment linked to contractility changes on standing.
Patent for alpha-1-antitrypsin to treat CFS.
Children with CFS/ME had profoundly reduced quality of life; 88% had infectious onset and 4% attended school full-time.
Peak VO2 percent predicted (99.3 vs 110.7, p=0.05) and peak oxygen pulse (12.4 vs 14.9, p=0.03) were lower in post-IM CFS than recovered controls.
IPAQ-short form correlated only weakly (r 0.28-0.43) with accelerometry in CFS and is not valid.
Network analysis of 16 plasma cytokines showed different co-expression topology in CFS, with attenuated Th1/Th17 and a Th2-skewed pattern.
PSG, actigraphy and self-report compared in CFS: objective sleep time matched subjective, but sleepiness, fatigue and non-refreshing sleep were not reflected by PSG or actigraphy.
Review treating XMRV in CFS as plausible pending replication.
After IV tryptophan, women with CFS alone, but not CFS+FM, showed an exaggerated prolactin response; no difference in men.
US healthcare providers were generally aware of CFS but had knowledge and attitude gaps.
Wheel exercise improved behaviour and lowered lymphocyte apoptosis in a stress-induced rat fatigue model.
Both submaximal and self-paced exercise triggered PEM, but neither changed elastase, IL-1beta or C4a acutely; post-exercise C4a flagged as marker of PEM.
Discourse analysis of online accounts of doctor interactions.
CFS had higher neuroticism and unhealthy perfectionism than controls.
Childhood victimisation modestly predicted worse function in CFS but not worsening over time.
Pressure pain thresholds were lower at all sites in CFS (3.30 vs 8.09 kg/cm2, p<0.001), including pain-free areas, indicating generalised hyperalgesia.
Raltegravir and other drugs inhibited XMRV replication in cell lines.
P3a latency circadian rhythm was disrupted in CFS and restored after electroacupuncture.
Longer illness duration associated with more adaptive coping but no difference in impairment.
DISC1 Ser704Cys Cys allele associated with increased CFS risk.
Longitudinal MRI over one year showed no differences in atrophy, white matter hyperintensities, CSF volume or cerebral/CSF flow in CFS.
Homebound CFS patients had more impairment and extreme fatigue than outpatients with stable symptoms over time.
Adolescent CFS had lower plasma ADH and higher plasma osmolality and renin activity than controls.
note: Renin raised, unlike the renin-aldosterone paradox in adults

finding: Spa-resort rehabilitation with physiotherapy and polyoxidonium reported as effective; no numbers.
Perspective article proposing a physical therapy management model including graded exercise.
No XMRV in archived PBMCs from 32 Dutch CFS patients and 43 controls.
Repeated overnight sampling found no pro-inflammatory cytokine upregulation (serum, PBL mRNA, stimulated function), with a small IL-10 increase.
Interviews with recovered adolescents revealed themes of loss and seeking understanding.
GPs lacked confidence in diagnosing CFS/ME and saw the label as potentially harmful.
Only baseline depression predicted poor outcome after multi-component CBT-based treatment.
No XMRV DNA in 299 samples; weak neutralising activity not specific.
Poly I:C produced reduced adrenal ACTH sensitivity and impaired feedback in an animal fatigue model.
After maximal CPET, 85% of controls recovered within 24 h versus none of the CFS patients; only 1 CFS recovered within 48 h.
Patients with MCS, CFS or FM had markedly lower SF-36 function than population norms, more with overlapping diagnoses.
CFS had 2.12-fold odds of metabolic syndrome (OR 2.12, 1.06-4.23) with a graded relationship.
No attentional or interpretation bias for illness words in CFS; greater mood volatility after rumination.
EGCG reversed behavioural and oxidative changes in a forced swim mouse model.
Neutrophil respiratory burst, NK cytotoxicity and CD56bright NK cells were reduced in CFS; red cell deformability, aggregation and fibrinogen were unchanged.
note: Small; NK replicates, RBC deformability contradicts

finding: No XMRV or MLV DNA in 186 UK CFS patients.
CBT reduced fatigue without changing actigraphic activity; activity change mediated about 1% of the effect.
Cluster analysis of fatigue types found heterogeneous subgroups by severity pattern.
Thesis developing a metacognitive beliefs questionnaire for CFS/ME; abstract truncated.
REM-to-wake transitions higher in CFS alone and several transitions higher in CFS+FM versus controls (same cohort as 22043126).

Readability of supplement leaflets for diabetes and CFS exceeded recommended reading levels.

Only 40% of medical textbooks covered CFS, on 0.09% of pages.
Patent for milnacipran in fibromyalgia, CFS and pain.
43-channel EEG source analysis separated CFS from controls with 72-83% accuracy, with lateralised cortical differences.
Systematic review of expressed needs: diagnosis, respect, information, strategies and social participation support.
Parvovirus B19 seroprevalence similar (75% vs 78%) but anti-NS1 IgG found in 41.5% of CFS vs 7% of donors (OR 9.42), and B19 DNA in 11 CFS vs 0 controls.
Replication: all 88 gene expression differences confirmed; genomic subtypes related to EBV and enterovirus antibody results.
CDC CFS continuing education program reached providers; online course produced 84% of certificates.
Activity logs show time spent fatigued linked to pain and fatiguing activity; meaningful activity linked to less fatigue.
Meta-analysis suggests acupuncture raises total effective rate (OR 4.56) in CFS.
note: Low-quality Chinese trials; publication bias likely

finding: Poly I:C produced reduced splenocyte activity, sphingomyelinase suppression and HPA axis disturbance in rats.
Patent for balneology and massage method.
Multiplex plasma cytokines: LT-alpha, IL-1a, IL-1b, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-12 higher; IL-8, IL-13, IL-15 lower; TNF, IFN-gamma, IL-2, IL-10, IL-17 not different.
note: Fletcher/Klimas; same cohort as network paper

finding: 3T proton MRS found no reduction of cerebral glutathione in ME versus controls (2.70 vs 5.19, NS).
Echocardiography in 53 CFS patients showed a small left ventricular chamber with low cardiac output in a considerable number; slender build common.
68% of CFS participants had sleep apnea/hypopnea; those with and without SAHS did not differ, so SAHS should not exclude CFS.
Description of a DVD and booklet teaching pacing.
Factor analysis identified three symptom phenotypes (musculoskeletal, and others) associated with severity.

population: Adolescent offspring of mothers with CFS
finding: CFS in 12% of offspring of CFS mothers vs 2% of controls (not significant); no group differences in fatigue, pain, sleep or fitness.
Patent for TLR3 agonists (dsRNA) in CFS.
Commentary on exclusionary conditions and diagnostic workup in unexplained fatigue.

ECG-derived sleep architecture agreed with manual PSG scoring for total sleep and RDI (R=0.89), not for slow-wave vs light sleep.
Original WPI report of XMRV DNA in 67% of CFS vs 3.7% of controls; retracted.
Cochrane review of Chinese herbal medicine RCTs for chronic fatigue; abstract truncated.

Italian CFS cohort demographics similar to international literature.
Validation of a Hebrew FibroFatigue scale in fibromyalgia patients.
Machine-learning comparison on CDC CFS SNP data; naive Bayes with wrapper feature selection performed best.
Qualitative study of family responses to parental CFS.
Serotonin receptor genotype and HLA-DRB1 alleles associated with age at onset and some symptoms; autoantibodies not.
Fennell crisis-phase patients had worse function, mood and coping than stabilisation or resolution groups.
CFS-like fatigue (CDC criteria without clinical confirmation) in 1.0% of 9062 respondents; chronic fatigue 30.5%; associated with obesity, analgesic use and low activity.

CFS patients scored higher on Type A behaviour than general population and cardiac patients.

Mean serum 25-OH vitamin D 44.4 nmol/L in CFS, lower than comparison groups.
note: Retrospective survey; seasonal and indoor confounding

finding: Vastus lateralis transcriptome showed altered mitochondrial, oxidative balance and fibre-type genes, and reduced nicotinic receptor component expression.

RAGE promoter and HLA-DRB1 haplotypes, notably DRB1*1301 (OR 2.79) and DRB1*1104 (OR 0.39), differed between CFS and controls.

Hypothesis that varicella-zoster infection of peripheral ganglia causes some CFS.
Activity-pattern complexity (entropy and fractal dimension) over 12 days was reduced in CFS versus matched controls.
Psychiatric comorbidity in 33 of 70 CFS patients did not influence outcome; 9 of 70 recovered at 2 years.
